name: OH-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+17 partisan lean makes the seat structurally Republican
Incumbent Michael Rulli has raised roughly $1.1 million to Kirtley's about $1,100
No public polls or expert ratings; prediction markets price Republicans near 94%
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Rulli's incumbency, and a fundraising gap of roughly a thousand-to-one leave Kirtley without any visible path; markets and district fundamentals alike point to a double-digit Republican win.
model.watch: Only an unexpected scandal involving Rulli or a sudden influx of outside Democratic spending would put this seat in play, and no signs of either are visible.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ohio's sixth district is deeply Republican territory, and first-term Representative Michael Rulli is seeking a full term with every structural advantage. The seat carries a strong Republican partisan lean, Rulli enters as the incumbent, and he has raised roughly $1.1 million for the race. Democrat Elizabeth Kirtley has reported about a thousand dollars in contributions, a level that signals a minimal campaign operation in a district already tilted heavily against her.

No public polls or expert ratings track this contest, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, and prediction markets give Republicans roughly a ninety-four percent chance of holding the seat. Nothing in the available evidence suggests a competitive race; the realistic question is the size of Rulli's winning margin rather than who prevails in this industrial and rural stretch along the Ohio River.
